# Model-independent beat analysis port

The working branch is `feat/model-independent-beat-analysis`. Its unchanged
production baseline is Mixxx **2.7.0-alpha**, commit
`0fffd3d0d07b755c34c1730f7b87afadd8f2be19`.
`gabba43/mixxx:feat/beat-this-variable-tempo`, inspected at
`1dfcdbf3bbf238713e0c1c4c6b1e907e8090d311`, was used only as a comparison source.
No merge or cherry-pick of that branch was performed.

## Dependency review and selected scope

| Component | Dependencies retained | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Constant/Auto clock fitting | Existing beat positions, BeatUtils, Beats | Port the mathematical clock fit and conservative drift/phase/density checks. |
| Audio grid evidence | Stereo PCM, standard C++, existing Beats | Port multi-band onset evidence, conservative phase alignment and Constant/Variable ranking. |
| Queen Mary refinement | Existing qm-dsp detection functions and the small onset refiner | Port evidence-backed harmonic/phase correction; preserve the unrefined Variable path. |
| Dense-map predominant BPM | Existing beat-marker representation | Port 16-beat estimates and duration-weighted dominant-tempo averaging without moving beat positions. |
| Mode settings and scheduling | UserSettings, AnalyzerTrack, existing preferences/menu | Add Auto/Constant/Variable, migration, per-track overrides and matching cache metadata. |
| Model/custom backend selection and worker lifecycle | External inference and model configuration | Exclude completely. |
| Downbeat storage and rendering | Protobuf changes, Beats extensions, waveform/UI changes | Exclude completely, including optional Queen Mary downbeats. |
| Benchmark/install infrastructure from the comparison branch | Additional scripts and inference-specific setup | Exclude; use focused native tests and the already prepared development environment. |

The relevant source history includes `e77caf4f08`, `9cf7215c28`,
`ec1ba0fd10`, `5ac98bd282` and `f0e8170521`. Changes were selected by dependency
and behavior, rather than taking those commits wholesale.

## Resulting behavior

- Only the existing Queen Mary and SoundTouch analyzers are registered.
  SoundTouch remains a BPM-only legacy analyzer; it does not acquire beat tracking
  or variable-tempo support.
- New profiles default to Auto. Profiles with the old explicit fixed-tempo
  setting retain Constant or Variable. Saving a mode preserves the legacy key;
  legacy setters override the new mode. Invalid persisted modes fall back safely.
- Auto fits a full-track constant clock before interpreting tracker jitter,
  isolated phase steps or metrical switches as tempo changes. Sustained drift and
  tempo changes retain a variable map. Audio evidence can reject or align a
  candidate; silence cannot provide positive evidence.
- Constant retains an explicitly constant grid. The source branch's full-track
  constant-clock fit is adapted to the ordinary Constant mode, without its
  external-prediction preservation flag. The boolean BeatFactory API and existing
  Variable smoothing remain available unchanged.
- Queen Mary uses low-frequency onset evidence to refine plausible half-time,
  double-time, 2:3 and phase errors. Variable mode skips that correction. Analyzer
  reinitialization clears results; silent/short input and repeated finalization
  are handled safely.
- Fast analysis is limited to Constant mode. Its final partial block is processed
  instead of silently discarded. Auto and Variable need the full recording.
- Existing locked/manual/imported-grid protection remains in place. Cache
  metadata records the analysis changes and accepts either resolved Auto grid
  representation. An unsuccessful analysis does not replace an existing grid.
- Dense variable maps report tempo using a 16-beat neighborhood and a weighted
  dominant bucket, avoiding single-interval timestamp quantization artifacts.
- The preferences page and reanalysis menu expose only the general tempo modes.
  Refreshing preferences blocks selection signals to avoid changing settings.

No worker, model, model dependency, Python inference requirement, download,
checkpoint/hash setting, custom-provider UI, downbeat label, new protobuf field,
waveform change or inference-progress interface is included. Dependency manifests
and lockfiles are unchanged. New helper code is used by the native analyzers or
their general grid-selection logic.

## Validation and baseline comparison

The development environment uses Debian 13, GCC 14.2, CMake 3.31 and Qt 6.8.2.
The unchanged baseline built successfully and passed all **1,265 enabled CTest
tests**; 38 upstream-disabled cases were not executed. Both QML startup smoke
tests passed. Use CTest's separate processes: running the entire baseline suite
in one process exposed pre-existing timer-ID range assumptions, shared
key-notation state and a QML singleton/style collision.

`src/test/beat_analysis_comparison_test.cpp` was compiled and run first against
the unchanged production baseline, then against this port. Its 24 cases feed
identical 64-second stereo PCM blocks to both analyzers in Constant and Variable
modes: 80/120/174 BPM pulses, accented 174 BPM, 120 BPM at 48 kHz, and a gradually
slowing 120 BPM pulse train. Baseline results and its test executable are retained
outside the checkout in `/workspace/mixxx-cloud/baseline`.

The reported timing error is the mean distance from known pulse times to the
closest generated beat, excluding the first and last four seconds. It measures
synthetic pulse alignment, not perceptual beat quality. SoundTouch provides only
BPM, so its implied zero-origin grid phase is not a beat-tracking quality score.

Additional tests cover Auto/Constant/Variable selection, metrical changes,
end-of-track drift, phase slips, fractional tempos, malformed beat sequences,
quantized dense maps, kick-pattern changes versus whole-pattern edits, soft-bass
crests versus percussive attacks, multiple sample rates and chunk sizes, silence,
reinitialization, locked/manual grids, fast-analysis boundaries, mode migration,
preferences and cache behavior.

The final application and test targets build successfully. All **1,330 enabled
CTest tests pass** (65 more than the baseline); the same 38 upstream-disabled
cases remain disabled. This includes the mode/preferences tests and both QML
startup smoke tests. The full final run completed in 77.76 seconds. The identical
24-case comparison also passed against both production versions.

### Measured comparison

| Analyzer / mode | Input | Baseline BPM | Port BPM | Baseline error (ms) | Port error (ms) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Queen Mary / Variable | accented174 | 86.9900 | 86.9900 | 172.414 | 172.414 |
| Queen Mary / Variable | drifting120 | 117.9600 | 117.9600 | 6.166 | 6.166 |
| Queen Mary / Variable | steady120 | 120.0200 | 120.0200 | 12.494 | 12.494 |
| Queen Mary / Variable | steady120_48k | 120.0100 | 120.0100 | 11.443 | 11.443 |
| Queen Mary / Variable | steady174 | 87.0100 | 87.0100 | 172.377 | 172.377 |
| Queen Mary / Variable | steady80 | 80.0100 | 80.0100 | 10.592 | 10.592 |
| Queen Mary / Constant | accented174 | 87.0000 | 174.0000 | 172.414 | 6.190 |
| Queen Mary / Constant | drifting120 | 118.0000 | 117.8648 | 96.421 | 92.600 |
| Queen Mary / Constant | steady120 | 120.0000 | 120.0001 | 11.406 | 7.662 |
| Queen Mary / Constant | steady120_48k | 120.0000 | 120.0000 | 10.625 | 6.904 |
| Queen Mary / Constant | steady174 | 87.0000 | 174.0000 | 172.414 | 6.213 |
| Queen Mary / Constant | steady80 | 80.0000 | 80.0019 | 10.952 | 7.211 |

All 12 SoundTouch measurements are identical to the baseline, including its
existing half/third-tempo limitations on these synthetic signals. All six Queen
Mary Variable-mode measurements are also identical. The two 174 BPM Constant-mode
cases improve from approximately 87 to 174 BPM, reducing mean pulse distance from
172 ms to about 6.2 ms. Constant-mode alignment improves on the steady 80/120 BPM
cases as well. Forcing Constant on the drifting signal still produces roughly
93 ms mean error; it is intentionally the wrong mode for that signal. Auto is
validated separately against steady and drifting audio and the grid/evidence
regressions, rather than being reported as a baseline mode that did not exist.

### Reproduction

From `/workspace`, use the prepared container wrapper:

```sh
bash /workspace/mixxx-cloud/run.sh bash /workspace/mixxx-cloud/configure-build.sh
bash /workspace/mixxx-cloud/run.sh ctest --test-dir build --parallel 4 --output-on-failure
bash /workspace/mixxx-cloud/run.sh build/mixxx-test \
  '--gtest_filter=Backends/BeatAnalysisComparisonTest.*' \
  --gtest_output=xml:build/beat-comparison-current.xml
```

These checks use synthetic audio and repository fixtures. They do not establish
accuracy on a representative music collection or validate real DJ audio/MIDI
hardware. Audio-evidence buffers add approximately 16 kB per second of input
before temporary filtering/event storage, and additional analysis CPU work.
